posts.hook: capitol hill runs on ai chatbots now, and nobody's really watching
posts.caption: a wyoming woman's lawsuit says grok turned one childhood photo into thousands of csam images, dario amodei calls for mandatory ai safety testing and warns of a "crisis of trust", and congress is using ai chatbots for official work with almost no oversight. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: a lawsuit says grok made thousands of csam images from one childhood photo
slides.desc: part of a widening class action lawsuit against xai over grok's role in creating it

slides.title: congress is using ai chatbots for official work, with basically no rules
slides.desc: copilot, chatgpt, gemini and claude are all cleared, oversight isn't

slides.title: dario amodei says open-weights alone aren't enough, warns of a "crisis of trust"
slides.desc: wants mandatory safety testing for every capable model, open or closed

slides.title: china is far more optimistic about ai than the us
slides.desc: 84% trust it there vs 32% here, per stanford's ai index

slides.title: nvidia is in talks to put up to $3b into openai's ohio data center developer
slides.desc: sb energy is heading toward its own ipo, maybe as soon as next month

slides.title: unitree's viral humanoid robots shipped 5,500+ units in 2025
slides.desc: the china robot maker behind those influencer videos is readying its ipo

slides.title: cloudflare is being accused of "ai psychosis"
slides.desc: critics say feature chasing is costing it stability and dev experience
